issues.label: Replication Crisis
issues.summary: Systematic failure to reproduce published findings across multiple scientific disciplines, revealing widespread problems with statistical practices, publication incentives, and methodological transparency that undermine confidence in the scientific record.

_authored.detail: Replication efforts consistently fail to reproduce original findings, indicating that the scientific memory system is storing unreliable information
Peer review fails to catch the methodological weaknesses and statistical errors that produce irreproducible results, indicating error-detection breakdown
Data analysis practices shift toward p-hacking and selective reporting as researchers face pressure to produce statistically significant results
Statistical inference is systematically misapplied through significance threshold fetishism, multiple comparison violations, and underpowered studies
Publication systems selectively disseminate positive results while suppressing null findings, creating a distorted scientific record
Funding incentives reward novel positive findings over replication studies, systematically defunding the verification mechanism of science

issues.label: Research Funding Collapse

Experimental designs are compromised by inadequate sample sizes, reduced controls, and equipment substitutions as budgets constrain methodological choices
Social science research disproportionately loses funding as limited budgets are redirected to perceived higher-priority STEM fields

_authored.detail: Hypothesis generation proliferates as both paradigm camps produce competing explanatory frameworks, generating more theoretical proposals than can be empirically adjudicated

Experimental designs become adversarial, with each camp designing studies to falsify the other's predictions rather than test their own
